# Package rwsapi


## get metadata 

First, retrieve the information that is necessary to build the request. The function metadata() will get the complete catalogue. You can specify *grootheid*, *parameter*, *compartiment* and other parameters that can be used in the internally  used function rwsapi::rws_metadata(). 


```{r}
source("r/RWS-API.R")

# remotes::install_github("wstolte/rwsapi")
# require(rwsapi)
require(tidyverse)

md <- rws_metadata(
  filterList = list(
      Compartimenten = T,
      Grootheden = T,
      Parameters = T,
      Eenheden = T,
      Hoedanigheden = T,
      Typeringen = T,
      BioTaxon = T,
      Organen = T,
      WaardeBewerkingsMethoden = T,
      ProcesTypes = T,
      Groeperingen = T
    )
)

catalogue <- md$content$locatielijst %>%
  full_join(md$content$aquometadatalocatielijst) %>%
  full_join(md$content$aquometadatalijst)
```


## Select the metadata for your needs

We are interested in light extinction data for the stations along the Terschelling transect. Let's see which station contain such data.

```{r}
mycatalogue <- catalogue %>% 
  filter(parameter_wat_omschrijving == "Extinctie in Oppervlaktewater in /m") %>%
  filter(grepl("Terschelling", naam, ignore.case = T))

mycatalogue$naam

```

## Prepare list for request


```{r}
l <- rwsapi::rws_observation_queries(
  mycatalogue,
  start_date = as.Date("2000-01-01"),
  end_date = as.Date("2025-12-31"))
```

## Get results for one row of metadata

```{r}
# Get data for one combination of location and parameter 
result_1 <- rwsapi::rws_observations(l[[1]])
data_1 <- result_1$content
```

## Get results for all rows

```{r}
# Get multiple data
result <- map(l, rwsapi::rws_observations)

data <- map(result, list("content")) %>% bind_rows()
```


## Visualize the observations

```{r}
data %>%
  mutate(tijdstip =as.POSIXct(tijdstip)) %>%
  filter(numeriekewaarde < 20) %>%
  ggplot(aes(tijdstip, numeriekewaarde)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = locatie.naam)) +
  scale_y_sqrt()


```


Special attention should be paid to the field "groepering.code"and "groepering.omschrijving" for the tested parameter WATHTE (waterhoogte). If groepering equals "NVT", the data are raw measurements or caculations. In any other case they are an aggregated form (e.g. extremes) of the measurements. 

Another tricky one is procestype. For most variables, this is "meting" (measurement), but it can also be "berekend" (calculated) or "verwachting" (expected), for example for water level (grootheid.code == "WATHTE").
